preconditions.description: The input size n must be between 3 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: All elements in the array a must be positive integers between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.
The input must consist of exactly two lines: the first line is n, and the second line contains exactly n space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and any('YES' in line for line in stdout.splitlines())) or (stdout.strip() == 'NO')
postconditions.description: The output must start with either 'YES' (if it is possible to make all elements equal) or 'NO' (if it is impossible).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and (m := int(stdout.splitlines()[1])) >= 0 and m <= n
postconditions.description: If 'YES', the second line must be an integer m (0 ≤ m ≤ n) representing the number of operations.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(len(line.split()) == 3 for line in stdout.splitlines()[2:2+m])
postconditions.description: If 'YES', each of the next m lines must contain exactly three distinct integers representing indices (1-based) of the operation.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(1 <= int(i) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines()[2:2+m] for i in line.split())
postconditions.description: If 'YES', all indices in the operations must be within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and (all_equals := all(int(x) == int(a[0]) for x in a)) or (all_equals := False) if 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: If 'YES', the operations must transform the array such that all elements become equal after at most n operations. Here, a is the parsed input array, and all_equals is true if all elements are equal.
The number of operations m must not exceed n if 'YES' is printed.
